evidence.pali: ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma tassā nadiyā dve sotāni tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchanti? Yañca, bhikkhave, tassa dīpassa uttarante udakaṃ, yañca dakkhiṇante udakaṃ – ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma tassā nadiyā dve sotāni tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchanti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ saddhindriyaṃ taṃ saddhābalaṃ, yaṃ saddhābalaṃ taṃ saddhindriyaṃ; yaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ taṃ vīriyabalaṃ, yaṃ vīriyabalaṃ taṃ vīriyindriyaṃ; yaṃ satindriyaṃ taṃ satibalaṃ , yaṃ satibalaṃ taṃ satindriyaṃ; yaṃ samādhindriyaṃ taṃ samādhibalaṃ, yaṃ samādhibalaṃ taṃ samādhindriyaṃ; yaṃ paññindriyaṃ taṃ paññābalaṃ, yaṃ paññābalaṃ taṃ paññindriyaṃ. Pañcannaṃ, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’’ti. Tatiyaṃ.
evidence.chinese_simplified: “比丘们，是何理趣，依此理趣，那条河可计为二流呢？比丘们，那岛屿北端的水，以及南端的水——比丘们，此即是理趣，依此理趣，那条河可计为二流。同样地，比丘们，信根即是信力，信力即是信根；精进根即是精进力，精进力即是精进根；念根即是念力，念力即是念根；定根即是定力，定力即是定根；慧根即是慧力，慧力即是慧根。比丘们，比丘修习、多修习这五根，由于诸漏已尽，便能于现法中亲自证知、现证无漏的心解脱、慧解脱而住。”第三经。
evidence.english: “And what, bhikkhus, is the reason by which that river comes to be reckoned as ‘two streams’? The water, bhikkhus, at the northern end of that island and the water at the southern end—this, indeed, bhikkhus, is the reason by which that river comes to be reckoned as ‘two streams’. In this very same way, bhikkhus, that which is the faculty of faith is the power of faith; that which is the power of faith is the faculty of faith. That which is the faculty of energy is the power of energy; that which is the power of energy is the faculty of energy. That which is the faculty of mindfulness is the power of mindfulness; that which is the power of mindfulness is the faculty of mindfulness. That which is the faculty of concentration is the power of concentration; that which is the power of concentration is the faculty of concentration. That which is the faculty of wisdom is the power of wisdom; that which is the power of wisdom is the faculty of wisdom. Bhikkhus, due to having developed and frequently practiced the five faculties, a bhikkhu, through the destruction of the taints, dwells having attained the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life.” The third.

entries.pali: Saddhābalādīsupi saddhādīni vuttatthāneva. Akampiyaṭṭhena pana balanti veditabbaṃ. Evametesu assaddhiye na kampatīti saddhābalaṃ . Kosajje na kampatīti vīriyabalaṃ . Muṭṭhassacce na kampatīti satibalaṃ . Uddhacce na kampatīti samādhibalaṃ . Avijjāya na kampatīti paññābalaṃ . Ahirike na kampatīti hiribalaṃ . Anottappe na kampatīti ottappabala nti. Ayaṃ ubhayapadavasena atthavaṇṇanā hoti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于信力等中，信等之义亦如前说。然应知“力”以不动摇为义。如此，于此等[力]中：不为不信所动摇，故为信力；不为懈怠所动摇，故为精进力；不为失念所动摇，故为念力；不为掉举所动摇，故为定力；不为无明所动摇，故为慧力；不为无惭所动摇，故为惭力；不为无愧所动摇，故为愧力。此为依二词之义释。
entries.english: In the terms beginning with the faith-power, 'faith' and the other terms have the same meaning as already stated. However, 'power' should be understood in the sense of being unshakable. Thus, among these: it is the 'faith-power' because it is not shaken by faithlessness; it is the 'energy-power' because it is not shaken by laziness; it is the 'mindfulness-power' because it is not shaken by forgetfulness; it is the 'concentration-power' because it is not shaken by restlessness; it is the 'wisdom-power' because it is not shaken by ignorance; it is the 'moral shame-power' because it is not shaken by shamelessness; it is the 'moral dread-power' because it is not shaken by lack of moral dread. This is the explanation of the meaning by way of both terms.

entries.pali: Vīriyaṃ pana indriyāni patvā vīriyindriyaṃ hotīti vuttaṃ, maggaṅgāni patvā sammāvāyāmoti, balāni patvā vīriyabalanti, piṭṭhidukaṃ patvā paggāhoti. Satipi indriyāni patvā satindriyaṃ hotīti vuttā, maggaṅgāni patvā sammāsatīti, balāni patvā satibalanti, piṭṭhidukaṃ patvā sati hotīti vuttā. Evaṃ ime dve dhammā catūsu ṭhānesu vibhattā.
entries.chinese_simplified: 再者，精进(vīriya)于诸根中，被称为精进根；于道支中，被称为正精进(sammāvāyāma)；于诸力中，被称为精进力；于背二法(piṭṭhiduka)中，被称为策励(paggaha)。念(sati)于诸根中，亦被称为念根；于道支中，被称为正念(sammāsati)；于诸力中，被称为念力；于助益二法(upakāraduka)中，被称为念。如此，此二法于四处被分别。
entries.english: Furthermore, energy, having reached the faculties, is spoken of as the 'faculty of energy'; having reached the path factors, as 'Right Effort'; having reached the powers, as the 'power of energy'; and having reached the pair of backing states, as 'exertion'. Mindfulness also, having reached the faculties, is spoken of as the 'faculty of mindfulness'; having reached the path factors, as 'Right Mindfulness'; having reached the powers, as the 'power of mindfulness'; and having reached the pair of backing states, it is spoken of as 'mindfulness'. Thus, these two states are divided into four instances.

entries.pali: 14 . Satindriyaniddese saraṇakavasena sati . Idaṃ satiyā sabhāvapadaṃ. Punappunaṃ saraṇato anussaraṇavasena anussati . Abhimukhaṃ gantvā viya saraṇato paṭisaraṇavasena paṭissati . Upasaggavasena vā vaḍḍhitamattametaṃ. Saraṇākāro saraṇatā . Yasmā pana saraṇatāti tiṇṇaṃ saraṇānampi nāmaṃ, tasmā taṃ paṭisedhetuṃ puna satiggahaṇaṃ kataṃ. Satisaṅkhātā saraṇatāti ayañhettha attho. Sutapariyattassa dhāraṇabhāvato dhāraṇatā . Anupavisanasaṅkhātena ogāhanaṭṭhena apilāpanabhāvo apilāpanatā . Yathā hi lābukaṭāhādīni udake plavanti, na anupavisanti, na tathā ārammaṇe sati. Ārammaṇañhesā anupavisati, tasmā apilāpanatā ti vuttā. Cirakatacirabhāsitānaṃ asammussanabhāvato asammussanatā . Upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇe jotanalakkhaṇe ca indaṭṭhaṃ kāretīti indriyaṃ. Satisaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ satindriyaṃ . Pamāde na kampatīti satibalaṃ . Yāthāvasati niyyānikasati kusalasatīti sammāsati .
entries.chinese_simplified: 14. 在念根的解释中，以忆念故为‘念’。这是念的自性之词。因其反复忆念，故为‘随念’。因其仿佛迎向而忆念，故为‘忆念’。或者，这只是通过前缀而加强的说法。忆念的状态即是‘忆念性’。然而，由于‘忆念性’也是三皈依的名称，为了排除此义，故再次使用‘念’一词。此处的含义是：名为‘念’的忆念性。因其能忆持所听闻、学习的教法，故为‘忆持性’。因其具有沉入（即进入）的意义，故为不漂浮的状态，即‘不漂浮性’。譬如，葫芦瓢等物漂浮于水面，不会沉入；但念于所缘则非如此。它会沉入所缘，因此被称为‘不漂浮性’。因其对长时所作、长时所说之事不忘失，故为‘不忘失性’。在现起之相与阐明之相上行使主导作用，故为‘根’。名为念的根，即是‘念根’。不为放逸所动摇，故为‘念力’。由于是如实的、导向出离的、善的念，故为‘正念’。
entries.english: 14. In the exposition of the faculty of mindfulness, 'mindfulness' (sati) is so called by way of remembering. This is a term for the intrinsic nature of mindfulness. By way of remembering again and again, it is 'recollection' (anussati). As if going towards an object, by way of remembering, it is 'recollection towards' (paṭissati). Or, this is merely a term augmented by way of the prefix. The mode of remembering is 'the state of remembering' (saraṇatā). Furthermore, since 'the state of remembering' is also a name for the three refuges, the term 'mindfulness' is taken up again to exclude that meaning. The meaning here is: the mode of remembering designated as mindfulness. Because it is a state of retaining what has been heard and learned, it is 'retention' (dhāraṇatā). Because it is a state of not floating about, in the sense of immersion which is designated as penetrating, it is called 'the state of not floating about' (apilāpanatā). For just as gourds and so on float on the water and do not penetrate it, mindfulness is not like that with regard to its object. For it penetrates the object; therefore, it is called 'the state of not floating about.' Because it is a state of not forgetting things done and said long ago, it is 'unforgetfulness' (asammussanatā). Because it exercises sovereignty in the characteristic of presence and in the characteristic of illuminating, it is a 'faculty' (indriya). The faculty designated as mindfulness is the 'faculty of mindfulness' (satindriya). Because it does not tremble on account of heedlessness, it is the 'power of mindfulness' (satibala). Because it is mindfulness that is actual, mindfulness that leads out, and wholesome mindfulness, it is 'right mindfulness' (sammāsati).

entries.pali: Tattha catūhi indriyehi cattāro puggalā niddisitabbā. Kathaṃ? Duvidho hi taṇhācarito mudindriyo tikkhindriyoti, tathā diṭṭhicarito. Tesu paṭhamo asubhe ‘‘subha’’nti vipariyesaggāhī satibalena yathābhūtaṃ kāyasabhāvaṃ sallakkhento bhāvanābalena taṃ vipallāsaṃ samugghātetvā sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamati. Dutiyo asukhe ‘‘sukha’’nti vipariyesaggāhī ‘‘uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāsetī’’tiādinā (ma. ni. 1.26; a. ni. 4.14; 6.58) vuttena vīriyasaṃvarabhūtena vīriyabalena paṭipakkhaṃ vinodento bhāvanābalena taṃ vipallāsaṃ vidhametvā sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamati. Tatiyo anicce ‘‘nicca’’nti vipallāsaggāhī samathabalena samāhitacitto saṅkhārānaṃ khaṇikabhāvaṃ sallakkhento bhāvanābalena taṃ vipallāsaṃ samugghātetvā sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamati. Catuttho santatisamūhakiccārammaṇaghanavañcitatāya phassādidhammapuñjamatte anattani ‘‘attā’’ti micchābhinivesī catukoṭikasuññatāmanasikārena taṃ micchābhinivesaṃ viddhaṃsento sāmaññaphalaṃ sacchikaroti. Subhasaññādīhi catūhipi vā vipallāsehi samudayasaccaṃ, tesamadhiṭṭhānārammaṇabhūtā pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhasaccantiādinā saccayojanā veditabbā. Phalaṃ panettha cattāri sāmaññaphalāni, catūhi cettha vipallāsehi caturāsavoghayogaganthaagatitaṇhupādānasallaviññāṇaṭṭhitiapariññādivasena akusalapakkho netabbo, tathā catūhi satipaṭṭhānehi catubbidhajjhānavihārādhiṭṭhānasukhabhāgiyadhammaappamaññāsammappadhānaiddhipādādivasena vodānapakkho netabboti ayaṃ sīhavikkīḷitassa nayassa bhūmi . Yo hi subhasaññādīhi vipallāsehi sakalassa saṃkilesapakkhassa saddhindriyādīhi ca vodānapakkhassa catusaccayojanāvasena nayanalakkhaṇo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso, ayaṃ sīhavikkīḷito nāma. Vuttañhetaṃ –
entries.chinese_simplified: 在此，应以四根解释四种人(puggala)。如何？贪行者(taṇhācarita)有两种：钝根者(mudindriya)和利根者(tikkhindriya)；见行者(diṭṭhicarita)亦然。其中第一种人，于不净中颠倒地执取为“净”，以念力(satibala)如实辨知身的自性，以修习力(bhāvanābala)根除那颠倒(vipallāsa)，趣入正性决定(sammattaniyāma)。第二种人，于苦中颠倒地执取为“乐”，如经中所说“对已生的欲寻，他不忍受”等，以作为精进防护的精进力(vīriyabala)消除对立法，以修习力破除那颠倒，趣入正性决定。第三种人，于无常中颠倒地执取为“常”，以奢摩他力(samathabala)令心得定，辨知诸行(saṅkhāra)的刹那性，以修习力根除那颠倒，趣入正性决定。第四种人，因被相续、聚合、作用、所缘的密集性所欺，于仅是触等法聚的无我(anattā)中，错误地执著为“我”(attā)，以四句空性作意摧毁那邪执(micchābhinivesa)，现证沙门果(sāmaññaphala)。应知，以净想等四种颠倒而有集谛(samudayasacca)，以作为其所依与所缘的五取蕴(pañcupādānakkhandha)而有苦谛(dukkhasacca)等，此即谛的结合(saccayojanā)。此处的果是四沙门果。于此，应通过四种颠倒，从四漏(āsava)、四暴流(ogha)、四轭(yoga)、四结(gantha)、邪行(agati)、贪(taṇhā)、取(upādāna)、箭(salla)、识住(viññāṇaṭṭhiti)、未遍知(apariññā)等方面，引导至不善品；同样，通过四念住(satipaṭṭhāna)、四种禅住、决意、与乐相应的法、无量心(appamaññā)、正精进(sammappadhāna)、神足(iddhipāda)等，引导至清净品(vodānapakkha)，这就是狮子游戏(sīhavikkīḷita)法门之地。凡是以净想等颠倒引导所有杂染品(saṃkilesapakkha)，以信根(saddhindriya)等引导清净品，并以四圣谛的结合作为引导的特征，此种特别的释义(saṃvaṇṇanāvisesa)即是所谓的狮子游戏。正如经中所说：
entries.english: Here, four types of individuals should be described by means of the four faculties. How? The craving-prone individual is twofold: one with dull faculties and one with sharp faculties; likewise for the view-prone individual. Among them, the first, who grasps the perversion 'beautiful' in what is foul, discerns the true nature of the body with the power of mindfulness and, through the power of development, uproots that perversion and enters the certainty of rightness. The second, who grasps the perversion 'pleasant' in what is suffering, dispels the opposing tendency with the power of energy—which is the restraint of energy spoken of in such passages as 'one does not tolerate an arisen sensual thought' (MN 2; AN 4.14; 6.58)—and, through the power of development, shatters that perversion and enters the certainty of rightness. The third, who grasps the perversion 'permanent' in what is impermanent, with a mind concentrated by the power of tranquility, discerns the momentary nature of formations and, through the power of development, uproots that perversion and enters the certainty of rightness. The fourth, deceived by the compactness of continuity, mass, function, and object, has the wrong adherence of 'self' in what is not-self, a mere heap of phenomena such as contact. Through attention to emptiness with its four aspects, he destroys that wrong adherence and realizes the fruit of recluseship. The connection to the truths should be understood thus: the truth of the origin is the four perversions, such as the perception of beauty; the truth of suffering is the five aggregates of clinging, which are their basis and object; and so on. Here, the result is the four fruits of recluseship. Furthermore, the unwholesome side should be led by the four perversions, by way of the non-full-understanding of the four cankers, floods, bonds, fetters, wrong courses, craving, clinging, darts, stations of consciousness, and so on. Likewise, the side of purification should be led by the four foundations of mindfulness, the four kinds of meditative dwellings, the determinations, the states partaking of happiness, the boundless states, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, and so on. This is the ground for the method of 'the lion's play.' For that special exposition, characterized by leading the entire side of defilement by means of the perversions such as the perception of beauty, and the side of purification by means of the faculties such as faith, through the application of the four truths—this is called 'the lion's play.' As it is said:

entries.pali: Evaṃ tisso pariyattiyo vibhajitvā idāni tīsupi piṭakesu yathārahaṃ sampattivipattiyo vitthāretvā dassento āha ‘‘vinaye panā’’ tiādi. Sīlasampattiṃ nissāya tisso vijjā pāpuṇātī tiādīsu yasmā sīlaṃ visujjhamānaṃ satisampajaññabalena kammassakataññāṇabalena ca saṃkilesamalato visujjhati, pāripūriñca gacchati, tasmā sīlasampadā sijjhamānā upanissayasampattibhāvena satibalaṃ ñāṇabalañca paccupaṭṭhapetīti tassā vijjattayūpanissayatā veditabbā sabhāgahetusampadānato. Satibalena hi pubbenivāsavijjāsiddhi, sampajaññena sabbakiccesu sudiṭṭhakāritāparicayena cutūpapātañāṇānubaddhāya dutiyavijjāya siddhi, vītikkamābhāvena saṃkilesappahānasabbhāvato vivaṭṭūpanissayatāvasena ajjhāsayasuddhiyā tatiyavijjāsiddhi. Puretarasiddhānaṃ samādhipaññānaṃ pāripūriṃ vinā sīlassa āsavakkhayañāṇūpanissayatā sukkhavipassakakhīṇāsavehi dīpetabbā. ‘‘Samāhito yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 4.99; 3.5; netti. 40; mi. pa. 2.1.14) vacanato samādhisampadā chaḷabhiññatāya upanissayo. ‘‘Yogā ve jāyati bhūrī’’ti (dha. pa. 282) vacanato pubbayogena garuvāsadesabhāsākosallauggahaṇaparipucchādīhi ca paribhāvitā paññāsampatti paṭisambhidāppabhedassa upanissayo. Ettha ca ‘‘sīlasampattiṃ nissāyā’’ti vuttattā yassa samādhivijambhanabhūtā anavasesā cha abhiññā na ijjhanti, tassa ukkaṭṭhaparicchedavasena na samādhisampadā atthīti satipi vijjānaṃ abhiññekadesabhāve sīlasampattisamudāgatā eva tisso vijjā gahitā. Yathā hi paññāsampattisamudāgatā catasso paṭisambhidā upanissayasampannassa maggeneva ijjhanti maggakkhaṇe eva tāsaṃ paṭilabhitabbato. Evaṃ sīlasampattisamudāgatā tisso vijjā samādhisampattisamudāgatā ca cha abhiññā upanissayasampannassa maggeneva ijjhantīti maggādhigameneva tāsaṃ adhigamo veditabbo. Paccekabuddhānaṃ sammāsambuddhānañca paccekabodhisammāsambodhidhammasamadhigamasadisā hi imesaṃ ariyānaṃ ime visesādhigamāti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 如此分别三教典后，现为详述三藏中各自的成就与衰损，而说‘于律中’等。在‘以戒圆满为依，得证三明’等句中，由于戒通过念、正知力及业所有智力而从烦恼垢中清净，并达圆满，故当戒圆满成就时，即能以强力助缘的状态，令念力与智力现起。由此当知，戒圆满是三明的强力助缘，此乃同分因圆满所致。以念力成就宿命明；通过在一切事务中熟练地以正知行事，成就与天眼智相应的第二明；因无违犯，具有舍离烦恼的自性，又以其作为导向解脱之强力助缘，通过意乐清净而成就第三明（漏尽明）。戒作为漏尽智的强力助缘，在没有先前已成就的定与慧圆满的情况下，此理当由纯观行阿罗汉(sukkhavipassakakhīṇāsava)阐明。依‘得定者如实了知’之语，定圆满是六神通的强力助缘。依‘由瑜伽而生广慧’之语，通过先前修行、亲近导师、地方语言善巧、受持、遍问等所培育的慧圆满，是各类无碍解的强力助缘。此处，因经中说‘依于戒圆满’，若有人因定力未彰显而不能成就全部六神通，则依最高标准而言，他并不具足定圆满。虽三明是神通的一部分，此处亦仅取由戒圆满而来的三明。犹如由慧圆满而来的四无碍解，对强力助缘具足者，唯有通过圣道才能成就，因其仅在道刹那证得。同样，由戒圆满而来的三明及由定圆满而来的六神通，对强力助缘具足者，亦唯有通过圣道才能成就。当知此等证得，唯有通过证得圣道才能达成。这些圣者的殊胜证得，与独觉佛及正等觉者对独觉菩提和正等觉法的证得是相似的。
entries.english: Having thus divided the threefold learning, now, by elaborating on the successes and failures in the three Piṭakas as appropriate, the Teacher says, 'But in the Vinaya,' etc. In such passages as, 'Relying on the accomplishment of virtue, one attains the threefold knowledge,' it is because virtue, being purified by the power of mindfulness and clear comprehension and by the power of the knowledge of ownership of kamma, is cleansed from the stain of defilements and reaches fulfillment. Therefore, the accomplishment of virtue, as it is being achieved, establishes the power of mindfulness and the power of knowledge by way of the accomplishment of a supporting condition; thus, its nature as a supporting condition for the threefold knowledge should be understood as arising from the accomplishment of a homogeneous cause. For by the power of mindfulness, the knowledge of past lives is accomplished; by clear comprehension, through familiarity with well-seen actions in all undertakings, the second knowledge, connected to the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, is accomplished; and by the absence of transgression, due to the nature of abandoning defilements, by way of being a supporting condition for turning away from the round of rebirth, and through purity of intention, the third knowledge is accomplished. Without the fulfillment of previously accomplished concentration and wisdom, virtue's nature as a supporting condition for the knowledge of the destruction of the taints should be demonstrated by the taint-destroyed dry-insight meditators. From the statement, 'One who is concentrated understands things as they really are,' the accomplishment of concentration is a supporting condition for the six direct knowledges. From the statement, 'Wisdom indeed arises from practice,' the accomplishment of wisdom, developed through prior practice, residence with a teacher, skill in languages, learning, questioning, and so on, is a supporting condition for the varieties of analytical knowledge. And here, because it is said, 'by relying on the accomplishment of virtue,' for one for whom the six direct knowledges in their entirety, which are an expansion of concentration, are not accomplished, for that one, by way of the highest distinction, the accomplishment of concentration does not exist. Thus, even though the knowledges are a part of the direct knowledges, the three knowledges are taken as those that come along with the accomplishment of virtue. For just as the four analytical knowledges, which come along with the accomplishment of wisdom, are accomplished for one endowed with the supporting condition only by means of the path—because they are to be obtained only at the moment of the path—so too, the three knowledges that come along with the accomplishment of virtue, and the six direct knowledges that come along with the accomplishment of concentration, are accomplished for one endowed with the supporting condition only by means of the path. Therefore, their attainment should be understood as occurring only through the attainment of the path. For indeed, these special attainments of these noble ones are similar to the attainment of the Dhamma of the enlightenment of Paccekabuddhas and of Sammāsambuddhas.

entries.pali: Tatthā ti aṅkurādippabandhasaṅkhāte bhūtupādārūpasantāne. Ta nti vijjāpāṭavādi. Aññassā ti bālakāle katavijjāpariyāpuṇanādito aññassa. Saṅkhārato añño taṇhādiko aññapaccayo .
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘于彼’(tattha)，即于名为‘芽等相续’之大种所造色(bhūtupādārūpa)的相续(santāna)中。‘学统’(tanti)指学识、善巧等。‘另一’(aññassa)，指于孩童时期所作之学识研习等之外的另一者。行(saṅkhāra)之外的他缘，即是贪爱(taṇhā)等。
entries.english: By ‘therein’ is meant in the continuity of primary and derived matter, which is described as the series beginning with the sprout. By ‘continuity’ is meant skill in knowledge and so forth. By ‘of another’ is meant other than the learning and thorough acquisition of knowledge done in childhood and so forth. Another condition, such as craving and so forth, is other than formations.

entries.pali: 19 . Nava balāni – saddhābalaṃ vīriyabalaṃ satibalaṃ samādhibalaṃ paññābalaṃ hiribalaṃ ottappabalaṃ ahirikabalaṃ anottappabalaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 19. 九力(bala)：信力(saddhābala)、精进力(vīriyabala)、念力(satibala)、定力(samādhibala)、慧力(paññābala)、惭力(hiribala)、愧力(ottappabala)、无惭力(ahirikabala)、无愧力(anottappabala)。
entries.english: 19. Nine powers: the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of wisdom, the power of moral shame, the power of moral dread, the power of shamelessness, and the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing.

entries.pali: 34 . Pañca balāni – saddhābalaṃ vīriyabalaṃ satibalaṃ samādhibalaṃ paññābalaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 34. 五力(balāni)：信力、精进力、念力、定力、慧力。
entries.english: 34. Five powers: the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, and the power of wisdom.

entries.pali: 40 . ‘‘Sattadhā tattha saṅgaho’’ti vatvāna puna taṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘saṅkappapassaddhi cā’’ tyādi vuttaṃ . Tattha vīriyaṃ navaṭṭhānaṃ sammappadhānacatukkavīriyiddhipādavīriyindriyavīriyabalasambojjhaṅgasammāvāyāmavasena navakiccattā, sati aṭṭhaṭṭhānā satipaṭṭhānacatukkasatindriyasatibalasatisambojjhaṅgasammāsativasena aṭṭhakiccattā. Samādhi catuṭṭhāno samādhindriyasamādhibalasamādhisambojjhaṅgasammāsamādhivasena catukiccattā, paññā pañcaṭṭhānā vīmaṃsiddhipādapaññindriyapaññābaladhammavicayasambojjhaṅgasammādiṭṭhivasena pañcakiccattā, saddhā dviṭṭhānā saddhindriyasaddhābalavasena dvikiccattā. Eso uttamānaṃ bodhipakkhiyabhāvena visiṭṭhānaṃ sattatiṃsa dhammānaṃ pavaro uttamo vibhāgo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 40. 说了‘彼处有七种摄集’后，为了再次显示彼义，才说了‘思惟与轻安’等。其中，精进有九处，即以四正勤、精进神足、精进根、精进力、精进觉支、正精进的方式，有九种作用；念有八处，即以四念处、念根、念力、念觉支、正念的方式，有八种作用；定有四处，即以定根、定力、定觉支、正定的方式，有四种作用；慧有五处，即以观神足、慧根、慧力、择法觉支、正见的方式，有五种作用；信有二处，即以信根、信力的方式，有两种作用。此是殊胜之三十七菩提分法中，最上等的分别。
entries.english: 40. Having stated, 'There is a sevenfold grouping here,' to further illustrate that, 'intention and tranquility,' etc., is stated. In this context, energy has nine instances: the four right exertions, energy as a basis of spiritual power, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, the enlightenment factor of energy, and right effort—thus having nine functions. Mindfulness has eight instances: the four foundations of mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, and right mindfulness—thus having eight functions. Concentration has four instances: the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and right concentration—thus having four functions. Wisdom has five instances: investigation as a basis of spiritual power, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, and right view—thus having five functions. Faith has two instances: the faculty of faith and the power of faith—thus having two functions. This is the supreme, excellent classification of the thirty-seven states distinguished by their nature as factors of enlightenment.
